newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Seven killed as Albanian violence continues.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed as Albanian violence continues.

text.p: Seven people have been killed in fresh violence in several Albanian towns, police said on Monday.
Two people were killed by masked gunmen at a cafe on the outskirts of the southern town of Vlore and two passengers on a passing bus were injured, acting police chief Haxhi Demiri said.

Frightened Vlore residents have refused to send their children to school although two armoured vehicles of the Italian-led multinational force, which is protecting aid supplies, were patrolling along the town's central boulevard.
Several regions of Albania are still on the edge of anarchy after the riots of February and March when thousands were left penniless by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Many pyramid schemes were based in Vlore, which was one of the key centres for rioting and violence.

In a separate incident, four people, including a woman and her five-year-old son were killed by stray bullets in the town of Memaliaj, 190 km (110 miles) from Tirana, as a gang of former prisoners unleashed machine gun fire into the air.
The gang had earlier clashed with police in the nearby town of Tepelene but had been driven back by police reinforced by other officers in armoured cars.
Violence was also reported in the north of the country on Monday, where one man was killed as gunmen tried to steal his car near the town of Shkoder, 110 km (60 miles) from Tirana.
The easy availability of weapons looted in the troubles, estimated at about one million, and the inability of the state to re-establish control in some regions is fuelling the continued violence.
